guide.title: Burns
guide.lead: Stop the burning, cool the burn, cover it and keep the patient warm. The burn itself rarely kills in the first hour; the airway and the smoke do. Estimate the size, look for inhalation, carbon monoxide and other trauma, and know who belongs in a burn centre.

steps.title: Stop the burning
steps.text: Remove from the source; power off for electrical; remove clothing and jewellery.

steps.title: Airway
steps.text: Hoarse voice, stridor, soot, facial burns: early ALS airway.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool running water for 20 minutes (useful up to 3 hours after the burn). No ice.

steps.title: Cover and warm
steps.text: Clean dry dressing or cling film; blankets.

steps.title: Size and fluids
steps.text: Large burns: lactated Ringer's at adults 500 mL/h, children 6–13 years 250 mL/h, 5 years or younger 125 mL/h.

sections.title: Rule of nines (adult)
notes: Infants: head 18%, each leg 13.5% (use a Lund-Browder chart for children).
Patient's palm with fingers is about 1%: good for scattered burns.

groups.title: Electrical
items: Small skin wounds, deep muscle damage

groups.title: Chemical
items: Brush off powder, then irrigate at least 20 minutes
Hydrofluoric acid: calcium gluconate gel 2.5%, cardiac monitor

sections.title: Burn centre
items: Partial-thickness 10% TBSA or more; any full-thickness
Face, hands, feet, genitals, perineum, major joints; circumferential
Electrical, chemical, inhalation; burns with trauma

quiz.q: Partial-thickness burns to the front of the trunk, the whole right arm and the front of the right leg. TBSA?
4-year-old with burns to the head and front of trunk. Best size method?
options: Lund-Browder chart (or child-adjusted rule of nines): children's heads are proportionally bigger

quiz.q: High-voltage contact: small charred hand wound, bigger foot wound, confused, frequent PVCs. Priority?
options: Hidden deep injury and cardiac irritability: monitor, IV access, rapid transport to a burn centre
The foot wound because it's bigger

quiz.q: 8% partial-thickness burns to both hands and the perineum from a chemical. Destination?
options: Burn centre: hands, perineum and chemical burns qualify whatever the size
quiz.explanation: Location and type matter, not just size.

quiz.q: How long should a burn be cooled?
quiz.explanation: Useful up to 3 hours after the burn.

quiz.q: A white, leathery, painless burn is:
Hoarse voice, singed nasal hair and soot after an enclosed-space fire:
options: Inhalation injury: early airway management, 100% oxygen
quiz.explanation: Swelling can close the airway quickly.

quiz.q: Dry chemical powder on the skin:
quiz.explanation: Then at least 20 minutes of water.

quiz.q: Prehospital starting fluid rate for a large burn in an adult (ALS):
quiz.explanation: Children 6–13 years 250 mL/h, 5 years or younger 125 mL/h.

quiz.q: Smoke-inhalation patient with collapse and low BP. Consider:

flashcards.question: Burn depths
flashcards.answer: Superficial: red, dry, painful. Partial-thickness: blisters, moist, very painful. Full-thickness: white, leathery or charred, painless.

flashcards.question: Rule of nines
flashcards.answer: Adult: head 9%, each arm 9%, front trunk 18%, back trunk 18%, each leg 18%, perineum 1%. Infant: head 18%, each leg 13.5%.

flashcards.question: Palm method
flashcards.answer: The patient's palm with fingers is about 1% TBSA: for scattered or irregular burns.

flashcards.question: Burn centre referral
flashcards.answer: Partial-thickness 10% or more; full-thickness; face, hands, feet, genitals, perineum, major joints; circumferential; electrical, chemical, inhalation; trauma; children; suspected abuse.

flashcards.question: Signs of inhalation injury
flashcards.answer: Enclosed-space fire, facial burns, singed nasal hair, soot, hoarseness, stridor, hypoxia. Early airway; 100% oxygen.

flashcards.question: Circumferential burns
flashcards.answer: Act like a tourniquet on a limb or restrict breathing on the chest: escharotomy in hospital.

flashcards.question: Electrical burns
flashcards.answer: Hidden deep damage; cardiac monitoring; arrhythmias; rhabdomyolysis (dark urine); fractures from muscle spasm.

flashcards.question: Dry vs liquid chemical
flashcards.answer: Dry: brush off first, then irrigate. Liquid: irrigate at least 20 minutes (longer for alkali).

critical.scenario: From a house fire: facial burns, singed nasal hair, soot in the mouth, hoarse voice. SpO₂ 91%, RR 26. About 27% partial-thickness burns.
critical.question: Most immediate threat and priority?

options.t: Inhalation injury threatening the airway: 100% oxygen, sit up, early ALS airway, burn centre with pre-alert
Pain: treat pain before anything else
Cool all burns for an hour on scene
options.f: Don't delay the airway or let him get cold.

critical.explanation: The window to intubate closes as swelling grows. Treat for carbon monoxide too.
critical.kpi: Prioritizes inhalation injury and airway in a burn patient

critical.scenario: Rust remover splashed on a forearm: pain 10/10 and worsening despite a rinse, skin turning white and firm, pulse irregular.
critical.question: Likely chemical and management?

options.t: Hydrofluoric acid: keep irrigating, calcium gluconate gel 2.5% per protocol, cardiac monitor, emergency transport
Simple acid: dry dressing and routine transport
options.f: Severe pain and arrhythmia suggest hydrofluoric acid.

critical.explanation: Fluoride binds calcium: deep damage and dangerous arrhythmias.
critical.kpi: Recognizes hydrofluoric acid exposure and its systemic risk

critical.scenario: Electrical panel shock: small palm wound, larger shoulder exit wound, confused, irregular pulse 124, dark brown urine, can't move the right arm.
critical.question: Three main concerns?

options.t: Arrhythmia (cardiac monitoring), hidden deep tissue and compartment injury, and rhabdomyolysis (fluids, burn centre)
Dress the wounds, splint the arm, treat as concussion
options.f: That misses the cardiac and muscle damage.

critical.explanation: Small skin wounds hide large internal injuries.
critical.kpi: Identifies the hidden dangers of electrical injury
